text:
emma: FYI seeing a bump in 429s and a lot of hits tagged project_id=null from hosted-api around 2026-03-19 09:12 UTC.
liam: example log?
emma: `2026-03-19T09:13:02Z warn route=complete status=429 origin=service-key id=sk_live_*** project_id=null org_id=org_123 tokens=42`
raj: so auth succeeded but we lost project attribution. are these org-scoped service keys by design?
emma: yes, customers create org-level keys to share across projects. previously we treated them as "unattributed" for billing. router seems to be sending them through the low-priority path which is rate-limited.
sara: we shouldn't silently pick a default project for access control. but for billing attribution it's reasonable to infer a project to avoid charging to "null" bucket. needs explicit audit trail.
liam: proposal: sticky attribution in router. first observed project for a key becomes preferred for routing/billing until changed. keep explicit project header or token claim highest priority.
raj: telemetry we need: attrib_status per key (explicit | sticky | unattributed), count tokens by status, sticky_assign_count per-key, and a flag when assignment source=backfill.
infra-bot: alert: hosted-api 429 spike us-east-1 at 09:14 UTC.
emma: rollout plan idea: 1) feature flag `sticky_project_attrib` default off; 2) implement sticky behaviour behind flag; 3) console: show "Preferred project" with button to pick or clear; 4) backfill job to seed high-confidence keys (>=80% of tokens to single project in 90d) annotated as source=backfill; 5) metrics: api_tokens_total{attrib_status=...}, sticky_reassigns_total; 6) alert if unattributed ratio >0.5% during canary.
sara: console UX: be explicit that changing preferred project only affects billing attribution, not permissions. record audit event `project_attribution_set` with actor=system/backfill/admin.
liam: canary idea: roll to 10% orgs for 48h. split test: half show prompt to ask admin to select preferred project, half apply sticky silently. measure support tickets and `unattributed` metric.
raj: backfill concerns: we must avoid flip-flopping on keys used across multiple projects. backfill only when confidence >=80% and mark sticky_ttl=30d before auto-lock; if conflict later, notify owner.
emma: quick mitigation: route org-scoped keys to a non-rate-limited "org-aggregation" pool temporarily while we implement attribution changes to avoid outages.
liam: agree but add quota guard so org can't bypass limits.
sara: legal: need to surface in invoices that attribution was inferred. billing team please add invoice metadata when sticky_assigned=true.
raj: prometheus rule draft posted below.

```
alert: UnattributedTokensHigh
expr: sum(rate(api_tokens_total{env="prod",attrib_status="unattributed"}[5m])) / sum(rate(api_tokens_total{env="prod"}[5m])) > 0.005
for: 10m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "Unattributed tokens >0.5%"
  runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/attrib
```
emma: next steps: I'll open RFC and assign owners: emma (prod), liam (router), raj (billing), sara (console/legal). create INF ticket for canary.
infra-bot: created INF-4890: "sticky-project attribution for org keys" assigned to emma.
liam: I'll sketch router changes + metric names. raj: i'll coordinate billing join and invoice metadata. sara: I'll mock console flow and audit events.
